candidate.answerReason: The smaller triangle has half the original area, so its side parallel to the original base has length \(\sqrt2\). The trapezoid median is half the sum of its bases.

methods.label: Use similarity and midsegments
methods.explanation:
The trapezoid occupies half the original triangle, so the smaller triangle occupies the other half. Because the dividing line is parallel to a side, corresponding angles are equal, and the smaller triangle is similar to the original triangle.

Let \(s>0\) be the length of the dividing segment. Corresponding areas of similar triangles are in the square of their corresponding side ratio, so
\[
\left(\frac{s}{2}\right)^2=\frac12.
\]
Therefore \(s^2=2\), and the positive length is \(s=\sqrt2\).

The median of a trapezoid joins the midpoints of its nonparallel sides. Its length is half the sum of the bases. To justify this, draw a diagonal and take its midpoint. Joining that point to the two leg midpoints produces two triangle midsegments. They are parallel to the bases, lie end to end along the trapezoid median, and have lengths half the respective bases.

Here the bases are \(2\) and \(\sqrt2\), so the median has length
\[
\boxed{\frac{2+\sqrt2}{2}},
\]
which is choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).
methods.levelReason: Similarity, area ratios, and triangle midsegments give a complete elementary geometry solution.
